candidates: When refactoring a diagram DB module (e.g., `*Db.js` / `*Db.ts` files under `src/diagrams/`) from module-level functions to a class, do not convert immutable constants — enum-like objects, lookup tables, or other data that never changes per instance — into instance properties. Keep them as module-level `const` exports or declare them as `static` class members. Instance properties of this kind can be accidentally reset by `clear()` and require an instance just to read a constant value.

When converting a diagram DB module to a class, do not pull private helper functions that have no dependency on `this` into the class as instance methods. Leave them as module-level functions, or if they must live in the class scope, mark them `static`. Converting a pure function to an instance method implies instance state is involved and misleads future callers.

When refactoring or reorganizing a module, audit all exported symbols for dead code and remove any that are no longer referenced anywhere in the codebase. Search the full repo before deciding to keep a legacy export — do not carry forward unused exports.

Proofread `describe` and `it` string literals in test files for copy-paste errors. When adapting tests from one diagram type (or feature) to another, verify that every occurrence of the original subject name in descriptions, comments, and variable names has been updated to match the new subject.

In vitest tests, use `assert(value instanceof SomeClass)` (with `assert` imported from `'vitest'`) for instance-type assertions rather than relying solely on `expect` checks. This narrows the TypeScript type for subsequent lines and produces a clearer failure message if the assertion does not hold.
